doc.name: worldlens: the corner cases no surveyed document happens to contain

$comment: Seven rules of the language need a document that decides them, and no surveyed site happens to. A TIE: the station stands at [0, 0] and the two presentation points sit 900 steps away on either side, so only the tie-break can choose, and `a0000000-…` sorts below `b0000000-…`. A CLOSED INTERVAL: the east-half region's edges fall exactly on two cell centres, which a half-open rule would drop. AN EMPTY LIST: one sector names nobody and one names the west point, so `exists` has to say whether an empty list is a statement. THE REFERENCE FORMS: one entity spells out every way the format names another entity — a bare identity, a {generator, key} derivation address, a flat list of both — beside the three spellings that name nothing: a template-local handle, which is a form of the reader's that expansion rewrites, and an [x, y] position and an array inside an array, which are no address form of the reader's at all and reach nothing rather than raising. A DOTTED COMPONENT NAME: the last entity carries both `go.marker` and `go`, and each spells out a `station` field at the same dotted path, so `ref(x, y, "go.marker.station")` has to say which name it read. ONE THING REACHED TWICE: one hub, three routes and two stops, where the first and the last route reach the same stop and the middle one reaches a stop of a lower identity — so a lens field over those rows has to say whether it drops the repeat and which order it keeps. A DERIVED FRAME: the stamp at the end puts a `frame` on a template internal, so expansion mints a frame nobody declared — and a world's own frame graph never holds one, because the pipeline builds that graph out of the declarations before any generator runs. Two frames deep on purpose, so a walk over `pose.frame` and `frame.parent` has a chain to climb.

entities.name: east half, edged on two cell centres
the sector that names the west point
the entity that names things every way the format allows, and two ways it does not
the entity that spells the same path two ways
the stop only the middle route reaches
the stop the outer two routes both reach
the hub the three routes leave
a template whose internal is a frame
the one stamp of that template
